OpenStax Biology 2e, 39.1 Systems of Gas Exchange
NYSDEC I FISH NY: Fish anatomy vocabulary (Lemon Fish handout)

note.text: A fish's smooth, pointed shape slips through water easily. Scales cover it like armor, and slime on top helps keep out germs.
The tail fin, or caudal fin, sweeps from side to side and pushes the fish forward.

steps.title: Fins
steps.instruction: Trace the four other fins: one on the back, one on the side, two underneath.

note.text: The back (dorsal) fin keeps the fish upright. The side (pectoral) and belly (pelvic and anal) fins help it balance and steer.

steps.title: Gill cover
steps.instruction: Trace the curved edge of the gill cover.

note.text: Under this bony flap, the operculum, are the gills. As water flows over them, they take in oxygen from the water.

steps.title: Lateral line
steps.instruction: Draw the lateral line along the side.

note.text: The lateral line is a row of tiny pores along each side. It lets the fish feel movement and vibration in the water around it.

steps.title: Head
steps.instruction: Dab the eye and nostril, then draw the mouth.

note.text: Fish smell with their nostrils, called nares, which help them find food. They don't use them to breathe.

steps.title: Label the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered part.

mistakes.Gills: The gills are hidden underneath. This bony flap is the gill cover.

commonMistakes.Lung: Most fish have no lungs. They get oxygen with gills.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: A fish lives where the water is murky and dark. Which part best helps it notice a predator coming?

options.feedback: Yes. Even when it can't see, it can feel the water move as a predator swims close, and dart away.
The tail fin helps it escape fast, but noticing the predator is the lateral line's job.
The gill cover protects the gills. It doesn't sense anything.
Scales protect the body. The lateral line senses movement in the water.
